failures.test: MISSING (no test exists). Adversarial probe (rt-choros 2026-06-10): a wire string whose `facet` carries a record payload must throw or be stripped. parseHandle facet field is cast wholesale (facet as Facet) with no validation — same opacity-bypass class as R-1, on the sibling field. Wire facet:{fields:[...],data:{ssn}} mints a branded ObjectHandle carrying the payload; assertVariableValue returns ok:true (brand short-circuit) and serializeHandle re-emits the ssn. FF-9 covers only the ref vector, not facet. The suite is green only because the vector is untested. Repro: parseHandle(JSON.stringify({tenantId:T,handleId:'x',ref:{kind:'record',tenantId:T,registryId:REG,recordId:REC},facet:{fields:['a'],data:{ssn:'in-facet'}}})) -> handle.facet.data.ssn==='in-facet'; assertVariableValue(handle)==={ok:true}; serializeHandle(handle) contains 'in-facet'.

MISSING (no test exists). parseHandle does not enforce the cross-tenant binding that makeHandle enforces (AC-6). Wire ref with tenantId != envelope tenantId is accepted by parseHandle but rejected by makeHandle with CrossTenantHandleError, making parseHandle a strictly weaker minter than makeHandle on the untrusted-wire path. No FF-9 test covers parseHandle tenant strictness. Repro: parseHandle(JSON.stringify({tenantId:T,ref:{kind:'record',tenantId:'<other>',registryId:REG,recordId:REC},handleId:'x'})) -> accepted; makeHandle({kind:'record',tenantId:'<other>',...},T) -> throws CrossTenantHandleError.
